My family has farmed this land for generations and I have done this work for 40 years. My hands know the soil. My husband's cousin works in the city now, so I manage most of the farm myself — I must keep things simple and steady.

I have 15 mu. I give 12 mu to the wheat-maize rotation — that is my main food and income. The other 3 mu I plant garlic. Garlic brings good money at market and I know it well.

For wheat, I use the same improved variety the seed shop in town has sold for years — I trust it. I apply base fertilizer before planting, then urea in spring when the plants start growing again. I water four times: once before winter freezes, once in early spring, once when stems are rising, once when grain is filling. Two pesticide sprays — one in spring for disease, one around heading. I rotary till after maize harvest to break up the stubble.

For maize, I direct seed into the wheat stubble right after harvest in June. No time to plough in summer heat. I buy hybrid seed from the cooperative — everyone around here does, yields are much better. I water twice when it looks dry. Two sprays for pests.

For garlic, I use my own saved cloves — I have been selecting the best ones for thirty years. I plough the 3 mu plot deep before planting in October. Garlic needs water often and I have the well so I water five times through winter and spring. I spray three times for fungal rot, which is the worst problem.

I do not change what works.
